notice: Checklist agreement is not accuracy. These are selected difficult cases plus a tiny random sample, reviewed without human adjudication.

limits: Provisional review of fifteen selected challenge passages; this is not human gold or an estimate of performance across the corpus.
Only the supplied source text establishes the reading. The checklist is a prompt for review and may omit important content.
File hashes identify the exact saved inputs and outputs reviewed. Outputs were not edited during review.
The review checks the meaning of roles and notes as well as predicates. A correct statement label can preserve a distinction even when the contract cannot type the statement’s own modality.
Mention lists are not exhaustive occurrence inventories. Some standalone pronoun mentions have no explicit entity link even where claims correctly resolve the speech turns.
The contract lacks a divine-speaker kind and a group-membership predicate. These limits are distinguished from wrong historical assertions.

reviewers.role: Independent source reader reviewing saved extractions not produced by this reader
limits: This is a provisional reading of the supplied source text, not human gold or historical verification.
The checklist was used after the source readings. Its restrictions were not treated as proof against an explicitly uncertain interpretation.
No biographies, commentary, other editions or unsupplied passages were consulted. Exact-file hashes bind this review to the saved input and output bytes.
All fifteen supplied passages and their outputs were read, including claims beyond the checklist. Structural validation was supplied separately; this review focuses on meaning.
Full statement and event spans frequently use mention kind name. The review records representative mention defects but is not an exhaustive token or mention-kind audit.
These selected difficult passages do not support a corpus-wide accuracy estimate.

reviewers.role: Independent source-based semantic reviewer of the twelve frozen random passage readings
limits: This is a provisional review, not human gold. Both the readings and this review may contain mistakes.
Only the saved random inputs and corresponding frozen outputs were used as evidence. No outside chronology, biographies, translations or unsupplied text were consulted.
Checks cover participants, relations, speech, alternatives, hypothetical versus narrated events, and important omissions across every supplied segment. They are not an exhaustive gold claim list.
Open pronouns and interpretation alternatives are not penalized merely for remaining unresolved. A quoted source span does not by itself preserve a missing claim or fix a wrong occurrence link.
Repeated mention omissions are concrete examples, not a complete count of all absent mentions. Duplicate mention records should not inflate coverage counts.
This tiny set cannot establish population accuracy. Pass counts summarize these selected checks only.
Input and output hashes identify the exact reviewed file bytes. Extraction outputs were not edited.

additional_findings.reason: The Hebrew האמר can continue Oshaya’s support or introduce an answer by the discussion. Setting voice=oshaya, adding counterevidence to his objection, and calling the teaching quoted inside that objection silently selects one unresolved speaker boundary. The source alone does not justify that certainty.

cases.summary: The alternate attributed authors are correct, but the surrounding citation is assigned to Oshaya with unwarranted certainty.

checks.reason: Yehuda’s transmission from Rav is separate from the story’s inner speakers and actions.

The students address Akiva, who replies with the Sinai tradition; that tradition is attributed to Moses without direct hearing.

The report uses reports_in_name_of without adding direct hearing or lifetime ordering.

additional_findings.reason: The divine interlocutor is typed person so that the contract permits speech and participation claims. The episode explicitly denies an assertion of humanity. This is a type-system limit, not a claim that God is a historical sage.

checks.reason: The relationship is student_of with subtype student_colleague and a note expressly distinguishing it from an ordinary subordinate student.

additional_findings.reason: The passage explicitly says that the formal מי בדיל מר wording was not used. The saved reading ends with the actual question and reply and drops this negative speech evidence, although it explains why the relationship is described as student-colleague.

The three legal inferences from Rav’s conduct appear as statement nodes, but only the crossing prohibition receives an explicit supporting claim. The permitted early Sabbath prayer and praying behind a teacher are not structurally tied to the inference, before its later qualification.

The account supporting Yose’s prediction in 1:2:5, that grain grew in fifteen days in Joel’s days and supplied the omer, has a Joel mention but no event or attributed claim.

additional_findings.reason: The anonymous third-of-Marheshvan rain-request ruling is omitted as a claim, although its statement entity exists. A claims-only reader sees the seventh-day view without its stated alternative.
The reported precedent in Joel’s days and the offering made from that grain are absent as claims. They should remain reported support for the prediction, not independent agricultural facts.

Repeated named mentions are not complete: the names in the long attribution argument of 1:2:3 have no mentions in that source, and Rabbi Yehuda’s new occurrence introducing the crop teaching in 1:2:5 is not separately anchored.

The rules_like object is the person yehuda, while the particular rule is only in the content role. The full record is issue-specific, but a projection of subject/predicate/object alone would turn it into general agreement.

cases.summary: The long remembered encounter and its uncertain pronouns are handled carefully. The anonymous competing date and a narrated precedent are missing, and mention coverage is incomplete.

checks.reason: Megillah 1:10:2 keeps Meir’s bull-offering rule separate from the rabbis’ rule and Ila’s explanation of the contextual difference.
Haggai’s possible killing in 1:10:4 remains a rhetorical warning, and מֹשֶׁה is not made a historical visitor. The two replacement stories are kept distinct from the hypothetical rules.
Kimhit, Shimon and Yehuda are retained with their family claims. Her seven sons are not said to serve on the same day, and her account of her conduct remains her own speech.

The story’s incumbent priest is linked to m9, whose first לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל occurrence in 1:10:5 is actually the hypothetical replacement’s disqualification. The correct story occurrence follows שֶׁאִירַע קֶרִי.

The opening rules in 1:10:5 say the first priest retains all priestly duties and the second is fit neither as high priest nor ordinary priest. The extraction gives them entities but no claims stating those rules.

additional_findings.reason: The first_priest entity and m9 point to the wrong לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל occurrence. That source span describes the hypothetical second priest’s ineligibility, not the incumbent in Ben Illem’s story. The narrative roles in c13–c14 are otherwise supported, but their person anchor wrongly crosses the legal case and the story.

The first priest’s retained duties and the second priest’s disqualification from both priestly roles are missing as claims. Only the later validity of service performed anyway is retained, losing the condition that makes that later ruling significant.
Repeated person mentions are incomplete, including Yohanan’s named statements in 1:10:4 and 1:10:5, each represented only through his earlier 1:10:3 mention.

cases.summary: The stories, women and hypothetical warning are largely preserved. A wrong repeated-word anchor joins the legal case to the story, and important priestly eligibility rules are missing.

checks.reason: Sheviit 10:4:5–6 keeps the adjacent-name transmission parses as interpretations rather than explicit source variants. Abahu’s transmission from Yohanan remains shared.
Zeira’s question to Abahu and Yose’s objection before Yaakov have the correct local directions. Rav’s description of instructing his household is conditional practice, not a dated gift event.
The challenge to Rav is followed by explanations, including the final distinction between legal duty and pious conduct. The salt client’s account is not silently assigned a buyer or seller identity.
The quoted acquisition rules in 10:4:6 are reduced to the broad acquisition_rule label. The actual conditions for acquisition in each domain are not extracted as claims.

additional_findings.reason: The baraita’s different acquisition conditions are present only inside a large evidence quote and a general statement label. The claims do not retain which acts suffice in the buyer’s, seller’s or deposit-holder’s domain.
Repeated named references lack mentions, including Zeira and Abahu in their direct question in 10:4:5 and Yaakov’s second named occurrence in the encounter with Yose in 10:4:6.

cases.summary: Transmission uncertainty, dialogue and the final qualification of Rav are sound. Detailed legal conditions and repeated mentions are incomplete.

checks.reason: Peah 3:3:1 keeps Yose’s separate-allocation ruling apart from the sages’ one-allocation ruling. האמהות is correctly kept as onion terminology, not human mothers.
Yaakov bar Bun’s transmission from Hanina and Bun bar Hiyya’s question to Mana are preserved without identifying the two Bun mentions. The plural reply addressees are kept visible.
The later explanation about storage is retained after the ownerlessness explanation. The brothers and partners of 3:4 are treated as hypothetical participants.

The brothers’ two allocations after division and one after reunion, and the two buyers’ joint versus separate tree allocations in 3:4:1, are not recorded as rules. c15 only records a generic division event.
The opening anonymous ruling that onion mother plants are liable in 3:3:1 is omitted. Yose’s exemption is recorded without the positive ruling it contests.

additional_findings.reason: The legal outcomes in 3:4:1–2 are missing. Generic division and harvest events do not preserve one versus two allocations or the stated restrictions on allocating between earlier and later portions. These are supplied text, not missing context.
האמהות של בצלים חייבות בפיאה is an explicit anonymous positive ruling. Keeping only Yose’s exemption loses the opposing position.
m14 and m15 duplicate the same להן occurrence to store both a plural audience and a candidate link. Coverage counts need one source occurrence with several possible referents.

cases.summary: People, speech direction and hypothetical status survive, but several explicit legal positions are missing despite the complete-for-supplied-text label.

checks.reason: Ketubot 11:7:2 preserves competing parses for both adjacent-name sequences. Aivo’s embedded parent and the generic women are retained separately from the sages.
Yose of Sidon’s teaching before Yirmeya and its conflict with fruit-only rights are preserved. The subsequent unqualified Yose is not automatically merged with him.
Hila’s repeated address to Yose remains reported speech. The teacher reading is explicitly marked interpretation; Mana’s answer about slaves is explicitly identified as a rhetorical reading.

Shmuel says אין מעשין אלא, limiting coercion, and the discussion then challenges this with secondary prohibited marriages. The coercion statement label loses that restriction and the intermediate challenge is missing.

additional_findings.reason: The limitation in אין מעשין אלא and the objection והא תנינן שניות with its reply are not represented. c20 only says coercion applies to certain forbidden marriages. The final question is preserved, but the steps connecting it to the restrictive ruling are lost.

The second רבי in רבי הילא רבי אמר לי supports the proposed my-teacher reading, but it has no distinct mention. Other repeated named occurrences, including the second Shmuel statement in 11:7:6, are also unrecorded as mentions.

The quoted rule in 11:7:6 says to appoint a provider for up to thirty days and then divorce with payment. The provider is represented as an entity, but the timing, obligation and payment are absent as claims.

cases.summary: The transmission and dialogue readings are cautious. The restrictive coercion rule and intermediate argument are incomplete; some quoted legal obligations and mentions are missing.

checks.reason: Bava Kamma 9:7:2 retains the dying wife, her husband and her daughter. Her ownership statement is her claim, and the daughter is not automatically made the husband’s child.
The case coming before Rav is not converted into a personal visit by the wife or husband. Rav’s principle is linked as support without inventing an explicit transfer judgment.
Generic family examples remain hypothetical. Yirmeya and Yose ben Hanina share the house ruling, while the later unqualified Yose remains a separate possible identity.

In 9:7:1 the lost-deposit and stolen-deposit cases have different testimony and repayment outcomes. Only the first demand, lost answer and oath are extracted; the second case and repayment differences are absent.
In 9:7:2 the no-deposit rule and the different returns to a woman, husband, slave, master, minor and father are not recorded as obligations, although those people have entities.
The father-and-son vow in 9:8:1 has different inheritance outcomes depending on its wording. Only their hypothetical kinship is extracted from that segment.

additional_findings.reason: The stolen-deposit answer, testimony, double payment and contrasting voluntary-confession payments in 9:7:1 are missing. The extracted lost-deposit exchange does not represent the second legal case.
The deposit rules in 9:7:2 are mostly an entity list without the stated obligations: refusal to accept, returns during life or after death, and the instruction to preserve value for the minor.
The different inheritance outcomes and redistribution instructions in 9:8:1 are absent as claims. The later house and asset rules do not replace this father-and-son case.
Repeated names are not fully anchored: Yirmeya’s second named occurrence in 9:8:2 lacks a mention. The second deposit case also has no separate depositor/keeper occurrence records.

cases.summary: The named household story is careful and preserves uncertainty. Large parts of the supplied legal cases are absent despite the complete-for-supplied-text label.
